ui.agentMessages.settings.section.role: settings section title and sidebar label
ui.agentMessages.settings.section.note: Names the feature with its product noun. This is the one noun every agent-messages surface uses; never 'team chat'. Reused for the sidebar rail item and the section heading.

ui.agentMessages.settings.description.length: One sentence; may wrap to two lines.
ui.agentMessages.settings.description.note: One sentence under the section heading. States that the agent exchanges messages with other members' agents inside the reader's organization; it is not a marketing claim.

ui.agentMessages.settings.off_by_default.note: Sits under the Enable action in state B. States the default plainly so enabling is understood as a choice.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.b_title.note: State B is an eligible account with no endpoint yet. The heading names the current state, the body says what enabling adds. Nothing here may claim the feature is already on.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.b_body.note: State B is an eligible account with no endpoint yet. The heading names the current state, the body says what enabling adds. Nothing here may claim the feature is already on.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.c_title.note: State C is an active endpoint. The heading is the shortest possible 'On'; the body states the two-way flow without implying a guarantee of delivery.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.c_body.note: State C is an active endpoint. The heading is the shortest possible 'On'; the body states the two-way flow without implying a guarantee of delivery.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.d_title.note: State D is the user pause. The body must keep three facts: traffic stops both ways, queued messages stay, and resume needs no new consent.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.d_body.note: State D is the user pause. The body must keep three facts: traffic stops both ways, queued messages stay, and resume needs no new consent.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.e_title.note: State E is a user opt-out. The body says turning on again records fresh consent, so the reader is not surprised by the consent text reappearing.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.e_body.note: State E is a user opt-out. The body says turning on again records fresh consent, so the reader is not surprised by the consent text reappearing.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.f_title.note: State F is an organization kill or a lapsed plan with a retained endpoint. The wire exposes no actor, so the copy names only 'your organization' and never guesses admin versus operations. History stays readable.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.f_body.note: State F is an organization kill or a lapsed plan with a retained endpoint. The wire exposes no actor, so the copy names only 'your organization' and never guesses admin versus operations. History stays readable.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.turned_o.role: neutral banner title for state F
ui.agentMessages.settings.state.turned_o.note: The plain statement of state F. It is neutral for both an organization kill and a lapsed plan, because the wire cannot tell them apart.
The only actor the wire can honestly name. Do not invent 'an administrator' or 'Radient operations'.

ui.agentMessages.settings.state.read_onl.note: Rendered beside the retained consent record in state F. It explains why the record has no edit or renew control there.

ui.agentMessages.settings.action.enable.note: A button label. Sentence case, verb first, no punctuation. The same action is labelled identically wherever it appears.

ui.agentMessages.settings.action.enable_.note: A button label. Sentence case, verb first, no punctuation. The same action is labelled identically wherever it appears.

ui.agentMessages.settings.action.pause.note: A button label. Sentence case, verb first, no punctuation. The same action is labelled identically wherever it appears.

ui.agentMessages.settings.action.resume.note: A button label. Sentence case, verb first, no punctuation. The same action is labelled identically wherever it appears.

ui.agentMessages.settings.action.turn_of.note: A button label. Sentence case, verb first, no punctuation. The same action is labelled identically wherever it appears.

ui.agentMessages.settings.local.label.note: Names the MACHINE-LOCAL preference, distinct from server consent. It is a switch label, two to four words, sentence case.

ui.agentMessages.settings.local.stays_en.note: Sits under the local switch in state C. Turning the local switch off must not read as revoking enrollment: the account stays enrolled on other machines.

ui.agentMessages.settings.saving.note: Shown while a settings write is pending. Keep it short enough not to resize the button.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.show.note: The disclosure control that reveals the served consent text verbatim. The text is server-authored; this label only opens it.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.versio.note: A field label for the consent version string, e.g. bridge_consent_v1. The value is machine text and is never translated.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.via.note: A field label naming the surface that collected consent.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.at.note: A field label for the consent timestamp.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.via_di.note: The value shown for consent collected by the one-time onboarding dialog.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.via_se.note: The value shown for consent collected by this Settings section.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.no_rec.note: Shown when an endpoint has no consent record. A factual absence, not an error.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.renew.note: A warning when the stored consent is no longer the served version. It must direct the reader to the enable/renew action, never claim consent covers the new text.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.unavai.note: Shown in state B or E when the served consent text could not be read. Enabling is disabled in that state; the sentence says nothing was enabled.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.change.note: The recovery sentence after a consent_version_unknown refusal. It asks for a fresh read and a NEW click; it must not imply an automatic retry.

ui.agentMessages.settings.allowlist.read.role: read-only note in the reach editor
ui.agentMessages.settings.allowlist.read.note: Shown when the status says read_only (state F). Explains why the level controls, add/remove rows and Save are disabled rather than letting the reader press a write the server refuses.

ui.agentMessages.settings.allowlist.agen.note: Names the identifier type on an allowed/blocked row. The wire carries only an endpoint id; this label makes the machine identifier honest rather than presenting it as a person.

ui.agentMessages.settings.allowlist.pers.note: Names the identifier type on a person-targeted row. The wire carries only an account id; do not invent a display name.

ui.agentMessages.settings.allowlist.iden.note: Explains that the input expects an agent endpoint id and shows its prefix. The id itself is never translated.
Explains that the input expects a person's account id and shows its prefix. The id itself is never translated.

ui.agentMessages.settings.error.no_chang.note: States that a failed settings read changed nothing, then asks the reader to retry for the current status. Never implies messages were disabled or enabled.

ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_.role: informational notice at the top of the Agent messages settings section, shown beside a button that opens the conversation
ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_.tone: sentence case, calm, second person; news, not an error
ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_.length: Two short sentences; may wrap to two lines beside a button.

placeholders.count: number of incoming agent messages waiting; a positive integer, never 0

ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_.note: Incoming messages from other members' agents are held on this computer because the reader's chief of staff (the designated assistant conversation) has never been used. Merely opening the conversation releases nothing: the reader has to send one message of their own in it, and the held messages are then delivered. 'Chief of staff' is the product's name for that assistant role; say it once here (the button beside it says it again) and never use the assistant's personal name. 'That conversation' is the chief of staff's conversation. Plural forms matter: 'it'/'them' follows the count. Never say the messages were refused, failed, read or lost.

ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_.role: informational notice at the top of the Agent messages settings section, shown with NO button
ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_.tone: sentence case, calm, second person; news, not an error
ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_.length: Two short sentences; may wrap to two lines.

placeholders.count: number of incoming agent messages waiting; a positive integer, never 0

ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_.note: The same situation as ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.chief_of_staff, for when this screen cannot tell which conversation is the chief of staff, so there is no button. It tells the reader where to find it instead: the conversation list in the app's sidebar. Sending one message of their own there releases the held messages; opening it alone does not. Never say the messages were refused, failed, read or lost.

ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.open.role: button label beside the waiting-messages notice
ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.open.length: Two to three words; must fit a small button.
ui.agentMessages.settings.hold.open.note: Opens the chief-of-staff conversation with its message box ready, so the reader can send the one message that releases the held messages. 'Message' is a verb here. A navigation action, not a confirmation; it sends nothing by itself.

ui.agentMessages.settings.default_on.b_t.role: settings heading when no endpoint exists yet under default-on
ui.agentMessages.settings.default_on.b_t.note: Replaces the opt-in 'off' heading. Must not offer or imply an Enable action. 'Team Bridge' stays in English.

ui.agentMessages.settings.default_on.b_b.role: settings body under the default-on not-yet-set-up heading
ui.agentMessages.settings.default_on.b_b.note: Says it turns on automatically and that nothing is sent when it does. No call to action.

ui.agentMessages.settings.default_on.e_b.role: settings body after the member turned Team Bridge off under default-on
ui.agentMessages.settings.default_on.e_b.note: Points to the consent text below and to the explicit turn-on-again path, without the word Enable.

ui.agentMessages.settings.action.turn_on.role: settings button to turn Team Bridge back on after turning it off
ui.agentMessages.settings.action.turn_on.note: The explicit way back after Turn off under default-on. Deliberately not named Enable.

ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.via_de.role: consent record value: how consent was collected
ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.via_de.length: Two or three words, shown in a small grid.
ui.agentMessages.settings.consent.via_de.note: Value for the 'Collected in' row when the runtime enrolled the member automatically.
